html:
Elijah ben Solomon Zalman, known as the Vilna Gaon, was a Jewish scholar of Vilnius and the leading authority on the Talmud of his time.

He held no official post and lived much of his life in study, but his learning made him the guide of the Jews of Lithuania. He led opposition to the new Hasidic movement, whose followers he thought put feeling before learning. His followers, the Mitnagdim, built the great yeshivas of Lithuania.

His fame helped make Vilnius the Jerusalem of Lithuania, a centre of Jewish scholarship and later of Yiddish culture. Some of his students settled in the Land of Israel. That world was destroyed in the Holocaust, above all at Ponary. See Lithuania and Judaism.
sum: Elijah ben Solomon Zalman, known as the Vilna Gaon, was a Jewish scholar of Vilnius and the leading authority on the Talmud of his time.
